base_model: M1A/M1B/M1C canonical (Stage 2 closure a544eee); Gate 1 + Interpretation Audit (7cf0fa3 / 795c559 / 7629dc4)
experiment: M2 Gate 2 — sign-placement generality gate: witness-aligned vs witness-opposed pointwise sign-reflected sign-changing mismatch
research_question: Keeping the absolute sign-changing mismatch profile identical (Delta_O = -Delta_A pointwise), does placing the positive mismatch over the historical canonical witness-support region (XA) versus outside it (XO) change rebound / recurrence / churn-like dynamics? Primary causal comparison XA <-> XO; KC is contextual reference only.

frozen_inheritance.selection: cumulative-excess argmax D(j) = F(j) - j/K, ties -> smallest index (canonical, untouched)
frozen_inheritance.removal: prefix removal, each swept bin scaled by (1 - alpha) (canonical, untouched)
frozen_inheritance.exact_stopping: stop when D_max <= 1e-12 (canonical exact tolerance, untouched)
frozen_inheritance.initial_state: canonical q_near bin probabilities, identical for XA / XO / contextual KC at a given K (shared; never regenerated per kernel)

XA.role: Witness-Aligned: positive mismatch over most of the canonical witness-support region, negative in Far (role name only, no claim rebound must occur)

XO.role: Witness-Opposed: negative mismatch over the canonical witness-support band, positive mismatch in the Far side (exact pointwise sign reflection of XA)

critical_control_property: Delta_O(x) = -Delta_A(x) on every analytic test point and every execution grid; hence same breakpoints, same regularity, same piecewise complexity, same pointwise absolute mismatch, same max absolute amplitude (1/6), same initial state, same controller, same stopping rule. The ONLY manipulated variable is sign placement.
discretization_rule: q_j = G(j/K) - G((j-1)/K) by exact evaluation of the analytic CDF on bin edges (ThrowDistribution.bin_probs); breakpoints 1/3, 2/3, 5/6 are NOT rounded to the grid; no midpoint sampling, no numerical integration, no renormalization beyond the canonical fp residue correction
tau_num_usage: floating validation only (static CDF checks, mass checks, decomposition residual, floating-boundary diagnostics); NOT a stopping tolerance
horizon_rule: H(K) = 10*K active rounds or exact stop, whichever first; censored observations recorded as 'not stopped within pre-registered Gate-2 horizon'; no extension, no non-convergence interpretation

switch_convention.definition: large boundary switch: |Delta a| > threshold (M1A.1 / M1C.4 convention)

classification_convention.mapping: N_R = 0 -> No rebound; N_R = 1 -> Isolated rebound; N_R >= 2 and S_R/K < 1 -> Short recurrent transient; N_R >= 2 and S_R/K >= 1 -> Long-span recurrent / churn-like transient (reporting convention as in Gate 1; full quantitative signature attached to every label)

witness_risk_semantics: E_t(j) = M_t Delta(j) - gamma_t(j) via the repository rebound_residual helper (M1C.3/M1C.5); j_risk = argmax_j E_t(j) with smallest-index ties; x_risk = j_risk/K; called x_witness only on actual rebound rounds; prefix-restricted argmax (j <= j*) retained as supplementary (raw argmax can land on structurally-impossible suffix positions where E(K) = -D_max); sign at risk = sign of Delta at x_risk classified positive/zero/negative at tau_num; any actual rebound witness not classified positive halts execution (indexing/logic gate)
support_migration_definition: per kernel, positive support XA (0 < x < 2/3) vs XO (2/3 < x < 1); share of risk locations with sign(Delta) = positive reported for (a) all active rounds, (b) top-25% R_t rounds, (c) actual rebound rounds, in raw and prefix-restricted views
kc_context_source: experiments/m2_gate1_generality/results/ (committed Gate 1 rows; no re-run, contextual reference only — XA-vs-KC is NOT sign-effect identification)

theory_verification.decomposition_identity: D_new(j) = D_TM_new(j) + M * Delta(j) on every active round vs the actual next state; max_abs_decomposition_residual <= tau_num
theory_verification.rebound_criterion: actual rebound iff exists j: M*Delta(j) > gamma(j); TP/TN/FP/FN with plain strict semantics; |worst excess| <= tau_num flagged numerical-boundary; unexplained non-boundary FP/FN halts interpretation

falsification_matrix.X1: XA recurrent, XO no/limited rebound -> positive mismatch placement relative to the evolving high-risk region materially affects recurrent rebound dynamics; long XA churn additionally supports 'everywhere-positive mismatch is not necessary for long recurrent dynamics' (not universal)
falsification_matrix.X2: XA and XO both stop quickly -> placing substantial positive mismatch over the historical canonical witness-support region is not sufficient to recover canonical long churn; weakens 'static witness-band alignment is sufficient'
falsification_matrix.X3: XA and XO both show similar recurrence -> static witness alignment has weak predictive power under counterfactual laws; trajectory-dependent state reconstruction may dominate (Working Hypothesis only)
falsification_matrix.X4: XO more recurrent than XA -> strong falsification: canonical historical witness distribution cannot be treated as a fixed intervention map; witness geometry is endogenous to the law-induced trajectory (not a theorem)

forbidden_drift: no third kernel, no breakpoint/amplitude/sign-boundary sweeps, no alpha/initial-state/stopping changes, no deadband, no smooth approximation, no a_crit generalization, no new long-run theorem, no Gate 3, no Stage 4 start
